cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Making & the Legislative Process
cards.back: A Bill must pass through both Houses of Parliament and receive Royal Assent to become an Act

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Making & the Legislative Process
cards.back: The legislative process starts with a Green Paper (consultation) then a White Paper (firm proposals)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Making & the Legislative Process
cards.back: A Bill goes through First Reading, Second Reading, Committee Stage, Report Stage and Third Reading in each House

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Making & the Legislative Process
cards.back: The House of Lords can amend and delay Bills but cannot block those passed by the Commons (Parliament Acts)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Making & the Legislative Process
cards.back: After passing both Houses, the King gives Royal Assent and the Act becomes law

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Making & the Legislative Process
cards.back: Influences on law making include: public opinion, pressure groups, media, events, EU law and the Law Commission

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Making & the Legislative Process
cards.back: The Law Commission is an independent body that reviews and recommends reforms to the law

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Making & the Legislative Process
cards.back: Pressure groups lobby Parliament and government to change the law in their area of interest

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Making & the Legislative Process
cards.back: Media campaigns and public opinion can influence law making — e.g. Sarah's Law following a high-profile case

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Making & the Legislative Process
cards.back: Law reform may be needed when the law is outdated, unclear, inconsistent or fails to protect people adequately

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Making & the Legislative Process
cards.back: Private Members' Bills allow individual MPs to propose legislation — though few become law

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Making & the Legislative Process
cards.back: Delegated legislation allows detailed rules to be made quickly without a full parliamentary process

cards.front: What should you know about gcse law exam tips — law making & the legislative process?
cards.back: 1. For Law Making & the Legislative Process questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Law Making & the Legislative Process 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
